notes: Unit-tested bin/subagent (819 lines pre-row, 11 functions per the brief; T792 adds a 12th, _resolve_model, extracted verbatim from main()'s inline deepseek/claude/pi/ollama branches so the provider-routing table could be tested without a subprocess or a dry-run round-trip -- an extraction, not a module restructuring; behaviour is unchanged for every valid input). Half A: all 12 functions have a live production caller inside this file and activity in the last 24-72h (T713/T662/T631/T437/T792) -- ZERO deletion candidates. Full Half-A table (purpose / caller / last-touched / vanish-noticed) and the Half-B should-statements are in tests/unit/test_subagent.py's module docstring; 54 test methods, all green under python3 tests/unit/run.py (300 total across all lanes' files, 0 failures/errors, 4 pre-existing expected-failures owned by other rows' test files). Two real defects found and FIXED in this row (red before, green after): (1) _pi_session_path collided at whole-second granularity -- two attempts of one task launched within the same wall-clock second produced the SAME session filename, silently overwriting the earlier attempt's session (exactly what T650/T662 exist to prevent); fixed by adding pid + a per-process monotonic counter to the timestamp (time.time_ns() alone still collided on this host between two calls a few instructions apart -- demonstrated in test_uniqueness_would_have_been_red_at_whole_second_granularity). (2) a bare `--model` flag with no value (parse_argv yields True, not a string) crashed the ollama branch with an uncaught TypeError from re.sub(pattern, '', True) instead of a clean 'is required' message; fixed uniformly across all three raw_model-taking providers inside the new _resolve_model. One CHARACTERIZATION recorded, not fixed (shared behaviour with src/managent/main.zig's canonicalizeModelTag, a cross-language contract outside this row's scope): an ollama tag outside OLLAMA_TAG_TO_CANONICAL is accepted via a :cloud-strip fallback with no validation against the canonical set. Two concrete registry entries land in that gap and are asserted directly (TestResolveModel.test_registry_table / test_characterization_fallback_can_yield_noncanonical_label): kimi-k2.7:cloud is documented in docs/infra/model-registry.md as returning 'Error: model not found -- do NOT dispatch' yet routes identically to its working sibling kimi-k2.7-code:cloud (plausibly the exact shape of the brief's 'two lanes exiting 0 in 38 and 64 seconds' incident); kimi-k2-thinking:cloud (retired per the same doc) is not in the table at all and the fallback silently returns a non-canonical label ('kimi-k2-thinking') instead of refusing. No disagreement found between any unit arm and tools/regression-subagent-resident-gate.sh's shell arms -- TestMemoryGateVerdict reuses that script's own fixture constants (TENANT_MB=8000, TOTAL_MB=49152, threshold 18432) and reaches identical admit/refuse verdicts for controls A-H; re-ran the shell script itself after the code changes and it still passes all 10 controls unmodified, as do regression-dispatch-verification.sh, regression-depth-enforcement.sh, regression-session-capture.sh, regression-token-capture.sh and regression-subagent-prompt.sh (the last only once WEIZIGO_AGENT_DEPTH is unset in the shell -- this leaf's own inherited depth=3 from being dispatched at the cap made every dry-run in that script hit the depth-cap refusal; not a regression from this row's edits, confirmed by re-running with the var unset). SEPARATE HARNESS FINDING, also fixed (blocking, not optional): tests/unit/_load.py's load() could not load bin/subagent (or bin/dispatch) at all before this row -- importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path) with no explicit loader returns None for an extensionless path (verified on Python 3.9.6 and 3.14.6), so `spec.loader` raised AttributeError before reaching any module code. Fixed by passing an explicit importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader; documented in _load.py's own docstring since it's shared infrastructure other rows' test files also depend on. Also noted (not changed): bin/subagent's module-level `dispatch_verify = _load_pinned_dispatch_verify()` shells out to git at import time by default (WEIZIGO_DISPATCH_VERIFY_UNPINNED=1, its own documented escape hatch, avoids this and is what tests/unit/test_subagent.py sets before loading); the import also does a permanent sys.path.insert for tools/ as a process-wide side effect. Both are pre-existing (T631/T677 era) and out of scope to change here. Followed T792's operator method literally: Half A (for/caller/last-touched/would-be-missed) gated Half B (should-statement, red-or-green, cleanup) for every function; nothing was tested that Half A marked a deletion candidate, because nothing was.
